chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the crucified one, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that my grandfather (peace be upon him) prayed Salat upon his uncle?' I said, 'I know that, but I do not understand it clearly.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I shall clarify it for you. If the face of the crucified one was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder; and if his back was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. For indeed, between the East and the West is the Qiblah. And if his left shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder, and if his right shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. And however he was inclined, do not cease to be by his shoulder, and let your face be towards what is between the East and the West, and do not face towards him nor face away from his back completely.' Abu Hashim said, 'And I have understood it, Allah willing! I understood it, by Allah!'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer (specifically funeral prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: How to position the Imam for funeral prayer when the deceased is crucified?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Salat al-Janazah for a crucified person, emphasizing that the Imam should stand by the shoulder and face the general direction between East and West to avoid directly facing or turning his back to the deceased. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of maintaining respect and proper orientation during funeral prayers, even when the body's position is irregular or elevated. The detailed instructions highlight the importance of precision in ritual practice, ensuring that the prayer is performed in accordance with the principles of Qiblah and bodily dignity.
